subject: Japanese timber hall scenery replacing the campus glass building
reference: User-provided Japanese timber hall garden visual, image(20261016-021928).png

observations: Current Great Buddha Hall is seven bays wide.
Official published dimensions are 57.012m wide, 50.480m long and 48.742m high.
sources.usedFor: Research context and seven-bay timber facade rhythm only. This campus hall deliberately has different dimensions and is not a reconstruction.

observations: Great South Gate uses a double hip-and-gable roof and large timber pillars above a stone plinth.
The temple identifies its construction as Daibutsu style.
sources.usedFor: Exposed timber, layered roof silhouette and stone podium architectural vocabulary, together with the user's visual reference.

observations: Museum exhibit documents historic temple roof tiles, including lotus-patterned and bucket-molded tile examples.
sources.usedFor: Rounded modeled tile ribs, separate eave bands and ridge courses rather than smooth flat roofing.

model.navigation: Decorative landmark beyond north garden fence, not a walk-in interior. Bounds metadata is exported for integration.

limitations: No claim of survey accuracy, temple replica, structural engineering accuracy or exact historical joinery.
Research source imagery is not copied or shipped; all runtime geometry/textures are generated locally from code.
